description_full: Teekay Corporation Ltd. provides crude oil marine transportation and other marine services worldwide. The company operates in two segments, Tankers and Marine Services. It owns and operates crude oil and refined product tankers. The company also offers ship-to-ship support services; tanker commercial management operation services; technical management; and operational and maintenance marine services. It operates a fleet of 34 double-hull tankers. It serves energy and utility companies, oil traders, oil consumers and petroleum product producers, government agencies, and various other entities that depend upon marine transportation. The company was formerly known as Teekay Corporation and changed its name to Teekay Corporation Ltd. in October 2024. Teekay Corporation Ltd. was founded in 1973 and is headquartered in Hamilton, Bermuda.

financial_summary: Teekay Corporation Ltd. is a small-cap energy business with a $1.2B market cap on $950M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at -7% over the past three years and -9% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome. Operating margins are expanding by +3.0pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at 40% against a 8% cost of capital — a 31-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat.

The business throws off $112M in free cash flow — roughly 12 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.08× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.4% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 37% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 2.9× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

growth: Revenue has compounded at -7.3% over 3 years, -12.2% over 5 years and -9.0% over 10 years, so the decline is easing, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 31%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 30.0% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded -35.0% a year over five years, short of the 5% durability bar.
Capex runs 2.2x depreciation (20.0% of sales), so it is building capacity for future growth.
own: Insiders own 36.6%, meaningful skin in the game, and institutions hold 55%.
Insiders have only sold over the past year (15 sales, net $7.6M sold).
It returns 6.4% a year to shareholders (less 0.7% of net share issuance).

people: With about 2,130 employees, each generates about $446K of revenue, 0.2x the Energy median, and revenue has fallen 5.4% a year across its filed history.
